written:
## 1. The numbers
Risk-on. Chip and AI shares led a rebound from last week's selloff, and the VIX fell sharply. Nvidia and the Fed rate outlook are keeping the tone cautious.

## 2. What moved and why
**Stocks surge as tech rebounds and crude slides**
Why it happened: Last week's wipeout came from worries that Democratic midterm wins could slow AI data-center construction. Buyers returned to beaten-down chip stocks, and Brent crude fell sharply.
Why it matters: Cheaper oil eases inflation fears, which matters while markets are pricing a possible Fed hike. The S&P 500 is still about 3.4% below its record.

**Nvidia slides as board probes CEO Huang**
Why it happened: Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation after reports of a possible foreign intelligence operation targeting its chief executive. Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship with a businesswoman alleged to have links to Chinese intelligence.
Why it matters: Nvidia is the AI trade's bellwether, so leadership uncertainty weighs on sentiment even while other chip stocks rally.

**US and Canadian yields split on jobs data**
Why it happened: U.S. October payrolls rose 165,000 against 59,000 expected. Canada lost 4,700 jobs and its unemployment rate reached 6.7%.
Why it matters: A strong U.S. economy keeps the Fed leaning hawkish, while weak Canadian data softens the case for Bank of Canada tightening.

## Deals
- **Acquisition: Strathcona Resources → Greenfire Resources** (C$2.7). , about C$2.7–2.9 billion including debt. The price includes about $550 million of Greenfire net debt. It consolidates two Alberta oil-sands producers.
- **Acquisition: Mitsui Chemicals → JSR** (US$11.6 billion). , about US$11.6 billion. Japan's state-backed Development Bank of Japan is taking part. It deepens Mitsui's semiconductor-materials business.
- **IPO: Anthropic → Nasdaq listing** ($80). , reportedly $80–100 billion raised at a $1.25–1.75 trillion valuation. The offering would test demand for AI after the selloff.

## 3. What's coming today
- 12:15 PM ET: Richmond Fed's Barkin speaks, for clues on the December rate path. Bowman also speaks then.
- 12:25 PM ET: Bank of England Governor Bailey speaks (17:25 UTC), for the global rate backdrop.
- 1:00 PM ET: Six-week Treasury bill auction, a read on short-term funding demand.
- After the close: Take-Two and Occidental Petroleum report, with Rocket Lab; KKR is also on the week's list.
- : Tomorrow: CPI at 8:30 AM ET, then CoreWeave results after the close. These will drive positioning today.

## 4. Canada corner
- The TSX was up about 1% in morning trading as tech recovered, and the domestic calendar is light this week.
- Weak jobs data keeps the Bank of Canada debate alive. Payrolls fell and unemployment hit 6.7%.
- RBC agreed to buy Australian asset manager Yarra Capital Management. The price was not disclosed.
- National Bank also announced a deal for Embark Student Corp. on Friday.

## 5. The takeaway
If someone asks you about markets today: it's a relief rally led by tech and lower oil, but a possible December Fed hike and Tuesday's CPI keep the market fragile.
Consulting angle: Nvidia shows key-person and geopolitical risk in AI supply chains. Firms that depend on one supplier or leader should have succession and second-source plans ready.
Accounting angle: Strathcona and Greenfire share a controlling shareholder (Waterous). An auditor would first ask whether IFRS 3 applies or the deal counts as a common-control transaction, then check how the acquisition is valued.

stories.title: Stocks surge as tech rebounds and crude slides
stories.why_happened: Last week's wipeout came from worries that Democratic midterm wins could slow AI data-center construction. Buyers returned to beaten-down chip stocks, and Brent crude fell sharply.
stories.why_matters: Cheaper oil eases inflation fears, which matters while markets are pricing a possible Fed hike. The S&P 500 is still about 3.4% below its record.
stories.full:
Last week's rout followed the U.S. midterm elections. Investors dumped AI and chip stocks and pushed the Nasdaq into correction territory before a partial recovery on Friday. Monday's move extends that bounce.

The S&P 500 is up 2.43% and the Nasdaq 2.74%. Energy was the only S&P sector in the red, and industrials led the rest. Brent has come down from above $112 at the start of the month amid uncertainty over the war with Iran. One report had AMD and Marvell each up roughly 9%.

Chipmakers, industrials and airlines-type oil consumers benefit from lower crude, while energy producers lose. A strategist quoted by CNBC expects the S&P 500 to stay rangebound through year-end, citing elevated oil and uncertainty over the Fed.

Watch Tuesday's CPI and CoreWeave's earnings, which will test whether the AI trade can keep its footing.

stories.title: Nvidia slides as board probes CEO Huang
stories.why_happened: Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation after reports of a possible foreign intelligence operation targeting its chief executive. Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship with a businesswoman alleged to have links to Chinese intelligence.
stories.why_matters: Nvidia is the AI trade's bellwether, so leadership uncertainty weighs on sentiment even while other chip stocks rally.
stories.full:
A committee of independent directors, advised by outside counsel, will lead the review. The board says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Nvidia says Huang intends to remain CEO during the investigation.

The shares fell as much as about six per cent and hit their lowest intraday level since March 31. A 4.3% drop would erase roughly $193 billion of market value. The stock had already fallen almost 20% over the past month in the broader AI selloff.

Most of the market shrugged it off, and many megacap tech names rose. Nvidia's suppliers and customers are the group to watch for contagion.

Next up is Nvidia's 17 November earnings report, which will show how management handles the issue and how investors react.

stories.title: US and Canadian yields split on jobs data
stories.why_happened: U.S. October payrolls rose 165,000 against 59,000 expected. Canada lost 4,700 jobs and its unemployment rate reached 6.7%.
stories.why_matters: A strong U.S. economy keeps the Fed leaning hawkish, while weak Canadian data softens the case for Bank of Canada tightening.
stories.full:
The U.S. 10-year yield is at 4.86%, up 2 bps, and Canada's is 3.65%, down 2 bps. Traders see 78% odds of a quarter-point Fed hike in December. The Fed raised rates in September and paused in October.

The gap shows up in currencies too. The Canadian dollar weakened to near 1.41 per U.S. dollar after the diverging jobs reports. A firmer U.S. dollar also raises costs for Canadian firms with USD debt, while exporters gain.

Tuesday's CPI is the next test. Forecasts call for 0.3% headline and 0.2% core month-over-month. A hot print would raise hike odds and could pressure equity valuations on both sides of the border. A soft one would support the rebound.

deals.full:
Strathcona: Greenfire holders can take 0.25 Strathcona share or C$11 cash per share. Strathcona closed at $36.34 and Greenfire at $7.93 on Friday. By my math, the cash option is roughly a 39% premium. Waterous Energy Fund owns 72% of Greenfire and 57% of Strathcona and backs the deal. Strathcona expects about $400 million of cash tax savings over four years. Shareholder meetings are expected in January 2027.

Mitsui/JSR: Mitsui plans to fund the purchase with borrowing, equity issuance and other measures. It expects about 40 billion yen of extra annual profit. It would be Japan's largest chemicals-sector acquisition. Questions have been raised about Mitsui's balance sheet.

Anthropic: That range is below earlier talk of nearly $2 trillion. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley reportedly lead a syndicate of 22 banks. The company reportedly aims to finish before Thanksgiving. The pricing will set a public benchmark for AI valuations.
